open_questions.topic: Defense-system prevalence bias: reference (ECOR) vs environmental isolates
open_questions.q: The Vassallo panel is 52 ECOR (mid-1980s human/animal enteric reference collection) + 19 UMB (urinary-microbiome clinical) isolates. How much of the 'novel 21 systems / 32 proteins' discovery is a property of E. coli defence biology generally, versus a sampling bias of laboratory-reference + host-associated strains? In particular, are the per-system carrier frequencies (mean 2.9/71, 14/21 detected in only the source strain) representative of environmental E. coli (soil, water, wildlife) or would a matched-size environmental panel expose either substantially more novel systems (broader accessory pool) or substantially more shared systems (different MGE ecology)?
open_questions.basis: Report Section 4.3 documents 21/21 systems present in >=1 panel strain but with mean 2.9/71 carriers, min 1, max 11 (PD-lambda-1). Section 1 explicitly notes >10,000 of 21,149 gene clusters exist in only 1-2 of the 71 strains. The critique section flags that most 'novel systems' are empirically singletons in the tested pangenome, which is compatible with rare-real-defence or with lineage-restricted mobile passengers. The 71-strain source panel is stated as ECOR + UMB clinical; no environmental (non-host-associated) isolates are represented, so panel composition may over- or under-count carriage.
next_steps: Assemble a size-matched (~70) environmental E. coli panel from ENA/BV-BRC filtered by isolation source (soil, freshwater, wildlife feces) with quality gates (N50, contamination CheckM) equivalent to the ECOR/UMB genomes.

Re-run the identical BLASTP presence pipeline (self >=98/>=90, ortholog >=70/>=70/<=1e-30, homolog >=30/>=50/<=1e-10) on the 21 representative proteins against the environmental proteome group; report per-system carrier frequencies alongside the ECOR/UMB numbers.

For any systems whose environmental frequency differs by >2x from panel frequency, inspect the flanking MGE context on environmental contigs to see if the carrier MGE class (prophage, IS island, ICE, plasmid) has shifted.
Cross-check by rerunning DefenseFinder / PADLOC on both panels to see whether the 21 systems' novel-vs-known status is stable across ecological source.

open_questions.topic: Novel defense-system discovery beyond the DefenseFinder curated set
open_questions.q: The paper identifies 21 novel systems, of which 18/32 proteins have no seed-cluster match in Gao et al. 2020 and the remaining 14 match at <35% identity in the majority. Since 2022, DefenseFinder / PADLOC catalogues have grown substantially. Two open questions follow: (a) How many of the 21 Vassallo systems are now folded into DefenseFinder families (i.e. their 'novelty' has been superseded by community curation)? And (b) Are there additional candidate defence systems in the same 71-strain panel and same defence-hotspot loci that Vassallo's tab-selection missed because they act against phages outside the T4/lambda-vir/T7 tested set (e.g. Mu, P1, T1, T5, N4, filamentous phages)?
open_questions.basis: Report Section 4.5 replicates the paper's own novelty figures verbatim from Table S4: 18/32 without prior Gao-2020 match; 14/32 with matches at <35% identity (9 of those 14 confirmed <35% by independent recomputation, range 26.2-76.7%). The critique section explicitly flags that C5 novelty inherits Gao 2020's coverage limits and is not an independent modern-catalogue audit. The paper's selection was against exactly 3 phages, all lytic dsDNA phages of the T-even / lambda / T7 families; the discovery is therefore inherently biased toward defences active in that phage-recognition space.
next_steps: Run DefenseFinder (>=v2.0) and PADLOC (current release) on FASTA files for all 32 Vassallo proteins; classify each as: (i) now a named DefenseFinder family, (ii) partial-hit / candidate, (iii) still unclassified.
For any Vassallo system now folded into DefenseFinder, note the family name and any newer publications that characterised it; update C5 novelty accounting.

Re-scan the 71-strain proteome database (already built in work/) with the full DefenseFinder + PADLOC HMM sets to enumerate additional candidate defence loci that Vassallo did not report; cross-reference with the 14 defence-hotspot loci from Section 4.2 to see whether any hotspot has been under-characterised.

Repeat a fosmid tab-style selection in silico by mining the 71-strain BV-BRC contigs for ~40 kb loci with >=2 DUF/hypothetical-cluster co-occurrences flanked by MGE signatures --- an unbiased predictor of Vassallo-style candidates, testable against the paper's 43-loci short list.

open_questions.q: The paper's central genomic thesis (replicated here as C4: 16/21 systems with MGE neighbours, 14/21 in defence hotspots) treats each system's carrier locus as a snapshot. The dynamic question is unresolved: what is the horizontal-transfer trajectory of these 21 systems across E. coli phylogroups and neighbouring Enterobacteriaceae? Do the flanking prophage/IS/ICE signatures represent (a) recent, still-mobile transfer with intact carrier MGEs, (b) ancient transfer with decayed/fossilised MGE remnants, or (c) hitchhiking on convergent-but-independent hotspot loci that recruit unrelated systems? Concretely: for each of the 21 systems, is the synteny of the ~10-gene defence-hotspot cassette conserved across carrier strains, or does the same defence protein appear in unrelated genomic neighbourhoods in different strains?
open_questions.basis: Report Section 4.2 gives homolog counts per system (max 11 for PD-lambda-1, mean 2.9/71); Section 4.2 also documents MGE neighbours (0-34) and defence-like neighbours (0-9). Section 4.2 notes that systems with 0 MGE neighbours (5/21) may reflect draft-assembly fragmentation --- so synteny across carriers is not systematically compared. The critique section flags that C4 uses annotation-keyword matches, not a dedicated prophage caller, and that a genuinely orthogonal (PHASTER / geNomad / VirSorter2) reannotation could shift MGE calls. No cross-carrier synteny comparison was run.
next_steps: For each of the 21 systems with >1 carrier in the 71-strain panel (7 systems by Section 4.2 table), extract the +/- 20-gene neighbourhood for every carrier strain and compute pairwise synteny (Mauve, clinker, or protein-level all-vs-all BLASTP + gene-order MCL).

Re-annotate all 21 carrier contigs with geNomad + PHASTEST (long-standard prophage callers) and classify carrier-MGE type (intact prophage / cryptic prophage / ICE / IS island / conjugative plasmid / composite transposon) with confidence scores; compare to the keyword-based C4 calls.

Extend homolog search from the 71-strain panel to the full BV-BRC E. coli genome group (>200k assemblies) with a stringent identity cut (>=70/70) to enumerate the full carrier set per system; build a per-system distribution across E. coli phylogroups (A, B1, B2, C, D, E, F, G).

For the 3-5 highest-carrier systems, build maximum-likelihood trees of the defence protein alongside a core-genome tree of the carriers and compare topologies to test HGT vs. vertical inheritance (tree-tanglegram or ALE reconciliation).

open_questions.topic: Ecological cost of defense-system carriage under phage-free conditions
open_questions.q: The paper demonstrates that these 21 systems confer defence against T4/lambda-vir/T7, but does not measure the cost of carriage under phage-free growth --- a critical determinant of whether these systems are maintained by frequent phage predation, purged in phage-free niches, or stably carried at low fitness cost. This is genuinely open in the field: for abortive-infection (Abi) systems in particular, the cost is expected to be nontrivial (spurious activation causes cell death), which predicts strong purifying selection against carriage in phage-scarce environments. Is there evidence from carrier-strain growth phenotypes, expression levels, transcriptional silencing, or dN/dS across close carrier pairs that constrains the fitness-cost hypothesis for any of the 21 systems?
open_questions.basis: The paper (Section 1 of report) explicitly used the 'tab' (T4-abortive) selection, which recovers both direct-immunity and abortive-infection systems --- so a subset of the 21 are expected to be Abi-type with associated carriage costs. Report Section 4.3 shows carrier frequencies are strikingly sparse (mean 2.9/71, 14/21 detected only in the source strain); the critique section flags that this could equally reflect real rarity or lineage-restricted mobile passengers. Section 4.6 (C6) documents that the wet-lab phenotype is not computationally reproducible (no SRA deposition), so cost measurements would be de novo work, not replication.
next_steps: Compile any published growth-rate / competition-assay data for E. coli strains carrying the specific 21 systems (Google Scholar + Europe PMC citing-articles search on Vassallo 2022, PMID 36123438); note carrier vs. cured-strain growth rates.

For each of the 32 Vassallo proteins, compute dN/dS against the closest ortholog in another carrier strain (PAML codeml or HyPhy BUSTED); interpret dN/dS >>1 as diversifying (phage-arms-race), dN/dS <<1 as strong purifying (functional constraint), dN/dS ~1 as relaxed selection (carriage cost with sporadic use).

Query available E. coli transcriptomic atlases (e.g. Colombos, EcoCyc RNA-seq compendium) for baseline expression of the 32 proteins in the source strains under standard growth conditions; low/silenced baseline expression is consistent with cost-managing regulation.

Design a targeted growth-rate + competition assay: clone each of the 21 systems (or a representative subset of 5) into a common E. coli chassis (MG1655) under native promoter, measure growth rate in LB and minimal M9 vs. empty-vector controls; report the cost per system.

open_questions.topic: Combinatorial anti-anti-phage evolution and phage-encoded counter-defence arms race
open_questions.q: The paper tests one system at a time against wild-type T4/lambda-vir/T7 and does not address the counter-defence side of the arms race. Two related open questions: (a) Do T4/lambda/T7 (or their close relatives) already encode counter-defence genes (anti-toxin mimics, methyltransferases, DNA-modification systems) that neutralise any of the 21 Vassallo systems, and if so, how does that constrain the effective in-nature defence spectrum? (b) When multiple Vassallo systems co-occur in the same carrier strain (i.e. in a defence hotspot), do they act additively/synergistically, or does phage-driven evolution select for co-occurrence patterns that reflect functional epistasis? The Section 4.2 table shows several strains carry 2+ systems (e.g. UMB0934 = PD-T4-1 + PD-T7-5; ECOR65 = PD-T4-2 + PD-T4-10; ECOR30 = PD-lambda-4 + PD-T7-3), which is a natural setting to test combinatorial defence.
open_questions.basis: Report Section 4.2 documents 14/21 systems in multi-defence hotspots (>=2 defence-like neighbours), and the per-system table shows several source strains carrying 2 of the 21 systems each (e.g. UMB0934, ECOR65, ECOR30). Section 4.6 documents no wet-lab reproduction; the paper tested each system in isolation. Section 4.5 documents that 18/32 proteins are entirely unknown to Gao 2020, so counter-defence-gene homologs in T4/lambda/T7 are unlikely to be well-characterised for the novel majority. Section 4.4 documents that CRISPR-Cas and RM are annotated in 71/71 strains (i.e. the classical defence layer is ubiquitous) --- so the Vassallo systems act on top of an already-defended chassis, and any 'novel' defence must be evaluated against phages that have already evolved to evade CRISPR/RM.
next_steps: Cross-reference the 32 Vassallo defence proteins against curated anti-defence protein catalogues (e.g. anti-CRISPR database, anti-RM database, PhageLeads / dbAPIS anti-defence entries) to enumerate any known counter-defence for these systems; flag any Vassallo system with a plausible phage-encoded neutraliser.

For T4, lambda, and T7 (all with excellent published genome annotations), run HMM searches with anti-defence family profiles and manually curate any hits that overlap the Vassallo defence-target space.

In the 71-strain panel, enumerate all pairs of strains that co-carry >=2 of the 21 systems; for each co-carriage pair, test whether the co-occurrence is enriched vs. a random-carriage null (Fisher's exact / hypergeometric across the 21x21 pair space).

For 2-3 co-carriage pairs (e.g. UMB0934 with PD-T4-1 + PD-T7-5), plan a follow-up in vitro experiment: challenge single-system vs. double-system fosmid constructs with each of the 3 phages plus a broader phage panel (T-series, coliphage HK97, lambda variants); report defence-score matrix and infer additive vs. epistatic effects.
